reasons: The tool-precision half STANDS: the heuristic keys on token adjacency ('SCOTUS' within 45 chars of a case name), not on whether a SCOTUS holding is being taught. Even a clean post-S7 entry ('*United States v. Chatrie* (4th Cir.) -> superseded by SCOTUS - see Key cases') would fire HIGH. The docstring's no-false-positive promise is violated by the bare-token branch.

REFUTATION PARTIALLY LANDS on the finding's premise, via attack angle (1): the O1 ticket's claim 'content verified correct - no content defect' is contradicted by audit row TEACH-01, which names these very lines (Exclusionary Rule :129 'narrated bullet', Standing) as SCOTUS holdings TAUGHT inside Recent developments - an N5 pedagogy violation routed injected:S7 (relocate at EXECUTE). Both flagged bullets narrate the SCOTUS outcome ('acquiring geofence Location History IS a search (Binding - SCOTUS)') inside the RD section. The treatment FACT is accurate; the PLACEMENT is the defect N5 exists to catch. On these two specimens the lint was right for the wrong reason.

Therefore: fix the lint (the heuristic must survive post-S7 clean descriptors) AND keep the content half on TEACH-01/S7's row (already dispositioned ADOPT in S7's Decision Log; relocation happens at EXECUTE under the planning-time content freeze). The O1 FP ticket closes only when both halves land.
residual_risks: A genuine SCOTUS entry phrased 'Foo v. Bar, on cert from the 9th Cir. - SCOTUS held...' would be suppressed (circuit ref precedes the token). Mitigation: such an entry almost always carries a U.S./S. Ct. reporter cite in the window (has_us branch untouched, still fires); the fixture must pin this shape.
Scanning only window[:tag.start()] (45 chars) rather than the whole pre-tag line is deliberate - the subject court parenthetical hugs the case name; widening the scan would over-suppress.
